key: And she said: ‘I will surely go with thee; notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thy honour; for the LORD will give Sisera over into the hand of a woman.’
s: When Barak will march against Sisera only if Deborah comes too, she agrees with a warning; Radak, on 4:9, reads the woman as Deborah herself, the victory then told under her name and not his, and Metzudat David, on 4:9, as Jael, so that all would know the deliverance came from the LORD.

evidence.gloss: [Radak, on 4:9, ‘into the hand of a woman’:] Some explain it as Jael, into whose hand Sisera was delivered, and say she spoke this by prophecy; but that does not fit the verse, which says ‘notwithstanding … shall not be for thy honour’. Rather its meaning is this: if I go, the glory will not be yours, for the deliverance will come through me, and they will say that into Deborah’s hand the LORD sold Sisera, and this deliverance will not be called by your name. … [Metzudat David, on 4:9:] And so she said: surely Sisera will be put to death by a woman, and that is Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, as the account will tell. If so, all will know that this was from the LORD’s hand, for not by strength does a woman prevail.

reason: verse.js ok, ref Judges 4:9 and at [214,9] match; the key is the first sentence of 4:9, ending at ‘woman.’’. Plain sense faithful: Barak will go only if Deborah goes (4:8) and she agrees with a warning (4:9); no four-word run from the key. Read the whole chapter 4 packet. Radak on 4:9 names and rejects the reading that the woman is Jael, and takes it as Deborah: the deliverance will be told as by Deborah’s hand and not called by Barak’s name. Metzudat David on 4:9 takes the woman as Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, so that all would know it was from the LORD’s hand, since a woman does not prevail by strength; hence no glory is left to Barak as captain. The two genuinely differ and the sentence names both without resolving (rule 5); each paraphrase stays within his words. Rashi has no comment on 4:9.
